sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.4722 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A1 and A2 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.107 of 2019 of Atchempeta Police Station, Guntur District, registered for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 420 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 26.04.2019 at 11.00 A.M., when the complainant inspected the Ramakrishna Cool Drinks Shop situated at Kothari Centre, Atchmepeta,
found the banned tobacco products and on interrogation, as the accused confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R. for the offences stated supra.
3.

Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 420 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J 05.09.2019 SS Kollipara Akhil Kumar vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 5 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14136553/
